verdict: A record quarter: revenue rose 15% to $4.27B as fees on client assets grew with markets and inflows, lifting profit to a record $666M.

follow100Note: The credit-loss line is positive because the bank booked an $8M benefit (a release of money set aside for loan losses), which adds to profit instead of subtracting from it. The Other and eliminations segment is negative, so the other segments add to more than $100 of every $100 before it is removed.

takeaways.title: Record revenue of $4.27B
takeaways.text: Net revenues rose 15% from a year earlier to a record $4.27B, driven by asset management and related fees, which grew 23% to $2.31B.

takeaways.title: Private Client Group did most of it
takeaways.text: The advisor business for individual clients brought in a record $3.06B, about 72% of total net revenues, helped by record fee-based account assets of $1.16T.

takeaways.title: Record profit of $666M
takeaways.text: Net income available to common shareholders was a record $666M, or $3.40 per share, up 10% from a year earlier.

oneTimers: Adjusted results exclude $37M of acquisition-related expenses, net of tax; on that basis net income available to common shareholders was $703M, or $3.59 per share.
footerNote: Financials adaptation for a bank plus broker-dealer: revenue is net revenues — total revenues of $4,739M minus interest expense of $470M — which is how the company reports its top line, and the business segments above are segment net revenues. Cost of revenue is the bank loan benefit for credit losses (-$8M; the bank released reserves rather than adding to them). Operating expenses are the noninterest expense lines excluding that credit provision, and operating income is pre-tax income ($862M), following the site's bank pattern.
